en.name: Poha
en.summary: Poha is parboiled rice rolled flat into papery flakes. Sealed in a cool dark cupboard it keeps about 6–12 months — deliberately shorter than the couple of years given for whole white rice, because flattening exposes the entire surface of the grain to air.
en.pantry: An airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard, away from the hob, gives about 6–12 months. Milled white rice keeps far longer, and the difference is purely mechanical: poha is rolled flat, so far more surface meets the air than in a whole grain, and it goes stale and faintly cardboardy long before rice would. It is also a favourite of pantry moths and weevils, so look for webbing before you soak a batch. Thick poha survives storage better than the paper-thin kind, which turns to dust at the bottom of the jar.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for poha, so none is given here. An airtight jar in the fridge is a reasonable home for an opened packet in a humid kitchen, since it deals with both damp and insects, provided the container seals well and you let it come back to room temperature before opening. Soaked poha is a different food: it is a wet rice product, so use it straight away rather than letting a bowl of it stand, and refrigerate any surplus at once.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for poha. Freezing a sealed bag for a few days is a practical way to settle pantry moths in a large purchase — poha attracts them more than most dry goods — but that is a pest measure, not a shelf life. Since the flakes are fragile, a bag handled in and out of a freezer also tends to break down into powder.
spoilage: Webbing, larvae, small moths or fine dust in the jar — the commonest reason to throw poha out.
A musty or damp smell, or flakes that have gone soft and limp.
A stale, cardboardy taste in the finished dish.
Flakes that have crumbled to powder, which means they are old and have been handled a lot.
tips: Buy thick poha if you store it for a while; thin flakes crumble.
Check for webbing before soaking — it is easier to see in the jar than in the bowl.
Rinse briefly and drain; poha soaks in seconds and turns to paste if left.
Decant into an airtight jar and date the lid.

faq.a: About 6–12 months in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard — less than whole rice, because flattening exposes the whole grain surface.

faq.q: Why does poha go stale faster than rice?
faq.a: Because it has been rolled flat. Far more surface is exposed to oxygen, so the flavour flattens long before rice would.

faq.q: How should soaked poha be handled?
faq.a: Rinse and drain it right before cooking — it soaks in seconds. Refrigerate any surplus straight away; it is a wet rice product.

zh.name: 印度扁米片
zh.summary: Poha 是把半熟處理過的米壓成紙一樣薄的米片。密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月——刻意比整粒白米的兩年短，因為壓扁把整顆米的表面都暴露在空氣中了。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、避光、遠離爐火的櫥櫃，約 6～12 個月。精白米可以放久得多，而差別純粹是物理性的：poha 被壓成薄片，接觸空氣的面積遠大於整粒米，所以它會在米還沒出問題之前，就先變得陳而帶紙板味。它也是穀蛾和米象的最愛，所以泡之前先看看有沒有絲網。厚片的 poha 比紙薄的那種耐放，後者放到最後常常在罐底碎成粉。
zh.fridge: Poha 沒有公布的冷藏期限，本頁也不給。潮濕的廚房裡，開封後裝密封罐放冰箱是合理的做法，因為同時處理受潮和蟲害；前提是容器密封確實，而且開封前先回到室溫。泡過的 poha 則是另一種食物：它是含水的米製品，請泡完立刻用，不要讓一碗泡好的米片放著，多的要馬上冷藏。
zh.freezer: Poha 沒有給冷凍數字。大量購買時把密封袋冷凍幾天，是處理穀蛾的實用做法——poha 招蟲的程度高於多數乾貨——但那是防蟲措施，不是保存期限。而且米片很脆，一直進出冷凍庫翻動，往往會把它弄成粉。
spoilage: 罐內有絲網、幼蟲、小蛾或細粉屑——這是丟掉 poha 最常見的原因。
有潮霉味，或米片變軟、失去脆度。
做出來的菜帶著陳味和紙板味。
米片碎成粉，代表它已經老了、也被翻動太多次。
tips: 要放一陣子就買厚片的；薄片容易碎。
泡之前先檢查絲網——在罐子裡比在碗裡容易看見。
快速沖洗後瀝乾；poha 幾秒就吸飽水，泡久了會變糊。
倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。

faq.q: 印度扁米片可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月——比整粒米短，因為壓扁把整個米粒表面都露出來了。

faq.q: 為什麼 poha 比米更快走味？
faq.a: 因為它被壓成薄片，接觸氧氣的面積大得多，所以風味平掉的時間遠早於米。

faq.q: 泡過的 poha 要怎麼處理？
faq.a: 下鍋前才沖水瀝乾——它幾秒就吸飽。多的立刻冷藏，它是含水的米製品。
